Thanks again for the demo last week. We agreed the next step is a short planning sprint so we can confirm feasibility for an on‑prem install behind our firewall and a VPC peering option for our dev/onboarding cluster. Also, we'll want the on‑prem package compatibility matrix — OS, package manager, kernel modules, and any kernel versions you require for our appliance. If you have a small checklist we can fill, that would be best.

Alex / Team — attaching a concise CSV template (same fields as the attached inventory stub you sent) so you can drop rows from your CMDB. Key fields we need from a networking perspective:
• VPC ID / Account ID
• Region / AZs used for staging and prod
• Subnet CIDRs and whether they are public/private
• NAT gateway IPs / elastic IPs used for outbound
• Any hop/proxy appliance IPs (traffic egress)
• Expected concurrent connections and peak token throughput per minute (rough)

If you can fill the CSV and return it, we can do a quick sanity check and map to required route table entries.

For the VPC peering flow: 1) Create peering request from your side with the VPC IDs, 2) share the console link, 3) we accept and present route tables for insert. If you have cross‑account IAM restrictions, note them in the sheet.

Marissa Cole
Network Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks — attaching a filled inventory CSV and adding clarifications inline.

A few notes:
- VPCs: prod and staging are in separate accounts; will include both IDs.
- Egress is SNAT via managed NAT gateway; we can reserve an Elastic IP for your peering if needed.
- We run an HTTP forward proxy for outbound traffic; our proxy sits at 10.10.128.45 and enforces TLS intercept for a small set of domains. We can exempt your endpoints if necessary.
- Peak: expecting ~800 concurrent requests initially during batch jobs; steady traffic < 100 qps otherwise.

We also need to confirm: will Redwood require inbound connections to our environment (i.e., will you initiate connections into our VPC) or do you prefer an outbound-only model with private endpoints on your side? That affects the firewall rules we'll need to open.

Tim Scott
Network Architect
Lumenix Therapeutics

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + inventory request

Hi Tim & Alex —

Thanks for the details. A couple of implementation notes from the on‑prem compatibility side:
1) We provide two deployment modes for customer‑managed environments: a lightweight containerized appliance (recommended) and a full VM bundle for air‑gapped installs. The container option requires Docker 24.x or Podman 4.x and kernel >= 5.10.
2) The installer performs outbound TLS connections to our control plane on port 443 for activation and health reporting. If you need strictly inbound‑only install, we can provide an offline activation token workflow but it adds 2–3 business days to schedule and verification.
3) For private endpoints: if you expose a private IP service in your VPC and peer to our staging VPC, we will accept outbound connections from our side to that private IP. Alternatively, we can expose private endpoints in our VPC and you initiate connections. Outbound‑only from your side is simplest for firewall teams.

Action items I propose:
- Lumenix returns the filled inventory (received, thanks).
- Confirm whether you prefer outbound‑only (Redwood peering/initiates) or you want Redwood to connect inbound into Lumenix.
- If outbound‑only: reserve an EIP we can use for peering verification. If inbound: share the public Bastion/IP list and expected ACLs.

I'll flag compatibility: your proxy TLS intercept will require us to whitelist the installer domain; otherwise use the offline activation.

Grace O'Connor
On‑Prem Product Lead | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rodriguez <alex.rodriguez@lumenix.com>, Tim Scott <tim.scott@lumenix.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + inventory request

Team — appreciate the fast turnaround. Summary / next steps before the kickoff:

1) Inventory: Received the CSV from Tim. Marissa will run a quick mapping exercise tomorrow and send back a small route table diff that shows the exact changes we expect for peering. (Marissa: target EOD 2028-05-30)

2) Peering model: Lumenix prefers an outbound‑only model from their side (they will not accept inbound initiated connections). Grace confirmed that works — we will expose private endpoints in our staging VPC and Lumenix will initiate.

3) Installer compatibility: Lumenix runs TLS intercept; Grace flagged the whitelisting requirement. Alex / IT: please whitelist installer.redwood-inference.com for the short bootstrap window or confirm you want offline activation.

4) Security / procurement note: Ben (copied) will own the SOC2 evidence and will request the standard attestation packet once we move to canary testing.

5) Kickoff: proposing Friday 2028-06-01 10:00 PT for a 60‑minute working session to review the mapping and finalize peering steps. I'll send the calendar invite and attach the two artifacts we referenced.

If anyone needs a separate network deep‑dive before Friday, say so and we'll schedule a focused call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into staging.

Irene Choi
Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference

rene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
